title: Reported speech: dice que, dijo que
summary: Pass on what people say and ask: dice que, dijo que, preguntó si, me pide que.
focus: Reporting statements, questions and requests, with the tense, person, time and place shifts
content:
## Dice que: same tense, new speaker

To pass on what someone says, use **decir que** + their sentence. With a reporting verb in the present (**dice**, **cuenta**, **explica**) the tense stays. Only the person shifts, so **yo** becomes **él / ella** and **mi** becomes **su**.

- Ana: «Estoy cansada.» → **Ana dice que está cansada.** (Ana says she's tired.)
- Leo: «Mi coche no funciona.» → **Leo dice que su coche no funciona.** (Leo says his car doesn't work.)

Other reporting verbs: **contar** (to tell), **explicar** (to explain), **comentar** (to mention), **asegurar** (to assure), **contestar** (to answer). A message passed on is **un recado**. English can drop *that*; Spanish never drops **que**.

## Dijo que: the tense steps back

When the reporting verb is in the past (**dijo**, **contó**, **explicó**), the verb inside usually steps back:

| they said | you report |
|---|---|
| present: «Estoy en casa.» | imperfect: **dijo que estaba en casa** |
| future: «Vendré.» | conditional: **dijo que vendría** |
| ir a: «Voy a salir.» | **dijo que iba a salir** |
| preterite: «Fui al cine.» | stays: **dijo que fue al cine** |
| imperfect, conditional | stay as they are |

If it is still true now, the present may stay: **me dijo que tiene dos hijos**. A further step back for the preterite is coming at B2.

## Time and place move too

Reported later or somewhere else, words of time and place move with the story:

| they said | you report |
|---|---|
| **hoy** | **ese día** |
| **mañana** | **al día siguiente** |
| **ayer** | **el día anterior** |
| **aquí** | **allí** |
| **este / esta** | **ese / esa** |

- Carlos: «Mañana trabajo aquí.» → **Carlos dijo que al día siguiente trabajaba allí.** (Carlos said he was working there the next day.)

Only shift what has really changed: reported the same evening, **mañana** is still **mañana**.

## Questions and requests

A yes/no question is reported with **preguntar si** (*whether*, no accent). A question word stays, **accent included**:

- «¿Tienes hambre?» → **Me pregunta si tengo hambre.**
- «¿Dónde vives?» → **Me preguntó dónde vivía.**
- «¿Cuándo llegas?» → **Me preguntó cuándo llegaba.**

An order or request is reported with **decir que** or **pedir que** + present subjunctive after a present verb:

- «Ven a casa.» → **Mamá me dice que venga a casa.** (Mum tells me to come home.)
- «Esperadme.» → **Os pide que la esperéis.** (She's asking you to wait for her.)

Reporting a request after **dijo** needs a new tense, which comes at B2.

vocabulary.example: Mi hermana dice que la película es muy buena.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My sister says the film is very good.

vocabulary.example: Pedro nos contó que su abuelo era pescador.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Pedro told us his grandfather was a fisherman.

vocabulary.example: La profesora explicó que el examen sería en junio.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The teacher explained that the exam would be in June.

vocabulary.example: Elena comentó que el restaurante estaba cerrado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Elena mentioned that the restaurant was closed.

vocabulary.example: El mecánico me aseguró que el coche estaría listo el viernes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The mechanic assured me the car would be ready on Friday.

vocabulary.example: Le pregunté por la fiesta y contestó que no podía ir.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I asked her about the party and she answered that she couldn't go.

vocabulary.example: Te dejo un recado: Juan dice que llega tarde.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Here's a message for you: Juan says he's running late.

vocabulary.example: Mi vecino me preguntó si necesitaba ayuda.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My neighbour asked me whether I needed help.

vocabulary.example: El camarero nos pide que esperemos un momento.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The waiter is asking us to wait a moment.

vocabulary.example: Nos explicó que ese día no trabajaba.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He explained to us that he wasn't working that day.

vocabulary.example: Prometió que volvería al día siguiente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: She promised she would come back the next day.

vocabulary.example: Me contó que el día anterior llovió mucho.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He told me it had rained a lot the day before.

vocabulary.example: Dijo que vivía allí desde pequeño.
vocabulary.example_meaning: He said he had lived there since he was little.

quiz.prompt: Marta: «Estoy cansada.» → Marta dice que ___ cansada.
quiz.explanation: With dice que (present) the tense stays the same; only the person shifts from yo to ella, giving está.
hints: A present reporting verb keeps the same tense.
Who is tired now: yo or ella?

quiz.prompt: Ayer Marta dijo: «Estoy cansada.» → Marta dijo que ___ cansada.
quiz.explanation: After a past reporting verb (dijo) the present steps back to the imperfect, so estoy becomes estaba.
hints: Dijo is in the past, so the present steps back one tense.

quiz.prompt: Luis: «Iré a la fiesta.» → Luis dijo que ___ (ir) a la fiesta, pero al final no fue.
quiz.explanation: After dijo que the future becomes the conditional, so iré becomes iría.
hints: After dijo que, the future becomes the conditional.
Ir is regular in the conditional, so add -ía to the infinitive.

quiz.prompt: Pablo: «Ayer perdí las llaves.» → Pablo me contó que ___ las llaves el día anterior.
quiz.explanation: In everyday speech a preterite stays a preterite and only the person changes, so perdí becomes perdió. The careful written form, the pluperfect (había perdido), comes at B2. Ayer becomes el día anterior.
hints: What happens to the preterite after contó que?

quiz.prompt: Hace un mes, Lucía me dijo: «Te llamaré mañana.» → Lucía me dijo que me llamaría ___.
quiz.explanation: A month later, her 'tomorrow' is long gone: mañana becomes al día siguiente.

quiz.prompt: Ana: «¿Tienes hambre?» → Ana me pregunta ___ tengo hambre.
quiz.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with preguntar si (whether), and this si has no accent.
hints: A yes/no question has no question word to keep.
The word for 'whether', with no accent.

quiz.prompt: El profesor: «¿Dónde vivís?» → El profesor nos preguntó ___ vivíamos.
quiz.explanation: A reported question keeps its question word and its accent: preguntó dónde vivíamos.
hints: The question word stays, and so does its accent.

quiz.prompt: Mi madre: «Llama a tu abuela.» → Mi madre me dice que ___ (llamar) a mi abuela.
quiz.explanation: An order reported with dice que takes the present subjunctive: me dice que llame. Tu abuela becomes mi abuela.
hints: An order, not a fact, so use the subjunctive.

quiz.prompt: Mi jefe: «Te lo prometo: el informe está bien.» → Mi jefe me ___ que el informe estaba bien.
quiz.explanation: Asegurar means to assure, and the boss insists it's fine. Preguntar would need si, pedir would need the subjunctive.
hints: He promises, so which verb means to assure?

conversations.title: The landlady called
conversations.scenario: Irene took a call from their landlady yesterday and passes the message on to her flatmate Dani.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Dani, ayer llamó la casera mientras estabas en el trabajo.
lines.meaning: Dani, the landlady called yesterday while you were at work.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Oh really? And what did she tell you?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Me dijo que el lunes venía el fontanero a arreglar la ducha.
lines.meaning: She told me the plumber was coming on Monday to fix the shower.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Por fin! ¿Te preguntó si estaríamos en casa?
lines.meaning: At last! Did she ask you whether we'd be at home?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí. Le contesté que yo estaría allí toda la mañana.
lines.meaning: Yes. I answered that I'd be there all morning.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Great. And did she mention anything about the rent?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, explicó que el año que viene el alquiler subiría un poco.
lines.meaning: Yes, she explained that the rent would go up a bit next year.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Cuánto? ¡Siempre nos asegura que es un piso barato!
lines.meaning: How much? She always assures us it's a cheap flat!

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No lo sé. Dice que la llames tú esta tarde.
lines.meaning: I don't know. She says you should call her this afternoon.
lines.note: An order reported with dice que: present subjunctive.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Vale, la llamo después de comer. ¿Algo más?
lines.meaning: OK, I'll call her after lunch. Anything else?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí: dice que el fontanero es muy puntual, así que no te quedes dormido.
lines.meaning: Yes: she says the plumber is very punctual, so don't oversleep.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Hey, she's saying that because of me!

listening.text: Mi primo dijo que tenía hambre.
listening.meaning: My cousin said he was hungry.
listening.note: Tengo becomes tenía after dijo que.

listening.text: Nos contó que el ascensor no funcionaba.
listening.meaning: She told us the lift wasn't working.
listening.note: New word: el ascensor = the lift.

listening.text: Mi jefa siempre me pide que llegue temprano.
listening.meaning: My boss always asks me to arrive early.

listening.text: Carmen comentó que ese día perdió el autobús.
listening.meaning: Carmen mentioned that she missed the bus that day.

listening.text: El médico me explicó que la herida era pequeña.
listening.meaning: The doctor explained to me that the wound was small.
listening.note: New word: la herida = the wound.

listening.text: Ayer Pablo me aseguró que vendría a la cena.
listening.meaning: Yesterday Pablo assured me he would come to dinner.
listening.note: Vendré becomes vendría after a past verb.

listening.text: Los vecinos nos contaron que iban a pintar la escalera al día siguiente.
listening.meaning: The neighbours told us they were going to paint the staircase the next day.
listening.note: New word: la escalera = the staircase.

guide.tip: Ask two things: is the reporting verb past (dijo) or present (dice)? And is it still today, here, for the same person?

bites.title: Dice que: same tense
bites.rule: With a present reporting verb (dice, cuenta, explica) the tense stays. Only the person shifts, for example yo to él and mi to su.
bites.example: Leo dice que su coche no funciona.
bites.example_meaning: Leo says his car doesn't work.

bites.title: Dijo que: step back
bites.rule: After a past verb, the present becomes the imperfect (estoy, estaba) and the future becomes the conditional (vendré, vendría). The preterite stays a preterite (fui, fue).
bites.example: Dijo que vendría y que estaba cansado.
bites.example_meaning: He said he would come and that he was tired.

bites.title: Time and place move
bites.rule: Reported later or elsewhere, hoy becomes ese día, mañana becomes al día siguiente, ayer becomes el día anterior and aquí becomes allí.
bites.example: Dijo que al día siguiente trabajaba allí.
bites.example_meaning: He said he was working there the next day.

bites.title: Questions and requests
bites.rule: Yes/no questions: preguntar si. Question words keep their accent (dónde, cuándo). Orders: dice que + present subjunctive.
bites.example: Me pregunta dónde vivo y me dice que vaya.
bites.example_meaning: She asks me where I live and tells me to go.

sorts.title: After dijo que, the verb becomes…
sorts.why: The present becomes the imperfect, the future becomes the conditional and the preterite stays.

sorts.title: A report or an order?
sorts.why: Passing on a fact takes the indicative; telling someone to do something takes the present subjunctive.

spots.sentence: Ayer Luis dijo que vendrá a la fiesta, pero no vino.
spots.why: After dijo que the future becomes the conditional.
A reported question keeps the accent of its question word.

spots.sentence: Ana me pregunta sí tengo hambre.
Mi madre me pide que llamo a la abuela.
Hace un mes Lucía dijo que me llamaría mañana.
spots.why: A month later, her 'tomorrow' is al día siguiente.

builds.text: Me dijo que tenía mucho trabajo.
builds.meaning: She told me she had a lot of work.

builds.text: Nos aseguró que lo haría al día siguiente.
builds.meaning: He assured us he would do it the next day.

builds.text: Ana dice que su hermano vive allí.
builds.meaning: Ana says her brother lives there.

builds.text: Le pregunté dónde vivía su hermana.
builds.meaning: I asked him where his sister lived.
